Aggregated index information for a variable: USR, definition payload, declarations, and use sites.

functions.name: ccls::Matcher::Matcher
functions.description: Constructs a string Matcher from the given pattern. Intended to prepare an internal matching implementation that can be used to test texts against the pattern. May throw on invalid pattern or allocation failure.
requirements: pattern must reference a valid std::string during the call
Construction may throw (as noted in header); callers should be prepared to handle exceptions if pattern can be invalid or memory allocation fails

functions.name: ccls::Matcher::~Matcher
functions.description: Destructor for Matcher. Releases any internal resources associated with the compiled pattern.
requirements: The Matcher object must not be used after destruction

functions.name: ccls::Matcher::matches
functions.description: Tests whether the provided text matches the Matcher's pattern. Returns true on match, false otherwise.
requirements: text must reference a valid std::string during the call

functions.name: ccls::GroupMatch::GroupMatch
functions.description: Constructs a GroupMatch consisting of a whitelist and a blacklist of patterns. Internally builds Matchers for each list to later test texts against these groups.
requirements: whitelist and blacklist must reference valid vectors of strings during the call
Construction may allocate and may throw on invalid patterns or allocation failure

functions.name: ccls::GroupMatch::matches
functions.signature: bool ccls::GroupMatch::matches(const std::string &text, std::string *blacklist_pattern = nullptr) const
functions.description: Checks if text is accepted by the group: typically requires matching the whitelist and not matching the blacklist. If blacklist_pattern is provided and the text is rejected due to a blacklist rule, the matched blacklist pattern may be written to it. Returns true if accepted, false otherwise.
requirements: text must reference a valid std::string during the call
blacklist_pattern may be null; if non-null it must point to a valid std::string to receive output

functions.name: ccls::hashUsr
functions.description: Computes a 64-bit hash for a USR-like string using an LLVM StringRef input. Intended for generating stable identifiers from symbol strings.
requirements: s must reference a valid character buffer for the duration of the call (per llvm::StringRef semantics)

functions.name: ccls::lowerPathIfInsensitive
functions.description: Returns a possibly lowercased version of the path if the filesystem or environment is considered case-insensitive. On case-sensitive systems, likely returns the input unchanged.
requirements: path must reference a valid std::string during the call

functions.name: ccls::ensureEndsInSlash
functions.description: Ensures the provided path string ends with a directory separator slash. Appends a slash if missing.
requirements: path must be a valid, mutable std::string reference

functions.name: ccls::escapeFileName
functions.description: Converts a file path into a filename-safe string by replacing directory separators with safe characters (e.g., replaces '/' with '_').
requirements: Input path is copied by value; no lifetime constraints beyond the call

functions.name: ccls::resolveIfRelative
functions.description: Resolves path against directory if path is relative; otherwise returns path unchanged. Produces a normalized absolute or combined path string.
requirements: directory and path must reference valid strings during the call

functions.name: ccls::realPath
functions.description: Resolves the real, canonical path for the given path (e.g., resolving symlinks and removing '.'/'..' where applicable).
requirements: path must reference a valid string during the call

functions.name: ccls::normalizeFolder
functions.description: Normalizes a folder path string in-place (e.g., adjusting separators, removing redundant components) and returns true on success.
requirements: path must be a valid, mutable std::string reference

functions.name: ccls::lastWriteTime
functions.description: Returns the last modification timestamp of the file at path as an integer time value, or std::nullopt if the time cannot be determined.
requirements: path must reference a valid string during the call
The file may or may not exist; absence or access errors result in std::nullopt

functions.name: ccls::readContent
functions.description: Reads the entire contents of filename into a string. Returns the content on success, or std::nullopt on failure (e.g., file not found or read error).
requirements: filename must reference a valid string during the call

functions.name: ccls::writeToFile
functions.description: Writes content to the specified filename, creating or overwriting the file as needed. No return value; errors are not reported via the signature.
requirements: filename and content must reference valid strings during the call
This function may overwrite existing files; callers should ensure this is acceptable
Error handling behavior is unknown from the header; callers cannot rely on return status

functions.name: ccls::reverseSubseqMatch
functions.signature: int ccls::reverseSubseqMatch(std::string_view pat, std::string_view text, int case_sensitivity)
functions.description: Performs a reverse subsequence match of pat against text, likely scoring or locating matches when scanning from the end. Returns an integer score or position; exact semantics are not documented.
requirements: pat and text must be valid string_view ranges for the duration of the call
case_sensitivity is an int flag; valid values are not documented in the header (commonly 0/1)

functions.name: ccls::hash_combine
functions.description: Base overload for hash combination: no-op when no more values are provided. Used to fold multiple values into a single hash seed.
requirements: seed must be a valid reference to a std::size_t accumulator

functions.name: ccls::getDefaultResourceDirectory
functions.description: Returns the default resource directory path used by the toolchain (e.g., for compiler resources).

functions.name: ccls::Maybe::valid
functions.description: Returns whether the contained T represents a valid value. Maybe<T> delegates validity to T::valid().
requirements: T must provide a valid() const method returning a truthy value indicating validity

functions.name: ccls::Maybe::operator bool
functions.signature: template <typename T> explicit ccls::Maybe<T>::operator bool() const
functions.description: Boolean conversion indicating whether the Maybe<T> currently holds a valid value, equivalent to valid().
requirements: T must provide a valid() const method (used internally)

functions.name: ccls::Vec::begin
functions.description: Returns a const pointer to the first element of the contiguous storage (or end if empty).
requirements: The Vec<T> instance must remain alive while using the returned pointer

functions.name: ccls::Vec::end
functions.description: Returns a const pointer one-past-the-last element of the contiguous storage.
requirements: The Vec<T> instance must remain alive while using the returned pointer

functions.name: ccls::Vec::size
functions.description: Returns the number of elements currently stored in the Vec.

functions.name: ccls::JsonReader::iterArray
functions.description: Iterate over the current JSON array, invoking the provided callback for each element while advancing the internal cursor. Typical usage is to push a value into a vector, then call reflect on it inside the callback.
requirements: this->m must point to a rapidjson::Value that is an array at the current position
fn must be callable without arguments and must safely process one array element per invocation
The function relies on internal state (m, path_); caller must not modify these concurrently

functions.name: ccls::JsonReader::member
functions.description: Locate a named member of the current JSON object and invoke the callback to parse/reflect its value. Used by reflectMember for JsonReader.
requirements: this->m must point to a rapidjson::Value that is an object at the current position
name must be a null-terminated string identifying the member to read
fn must be callable and should read/reflect the located member value
Member lookup updates internal path_ for diagnostics

functions.name: ccls::JsonReader::isNull
functions.description: Return whether the current JSON value at the reader's position is null. Commonly used to decide whether to emplace optionals.
requirements: this->m must be a valid rapidjson::Value pointer
Must be called when positioned at a single value (not necessarily object/array)

functions.name: ccls::JsonReader::getString
functions.description: Extract the current JSON value as a UTF-8 string. Used by reflect for string-like fields.
requirements: this->m must reference a JSON string value; behavior for non-strings is unspecified in this header
Returns a newly constructed std::string

functions.name: ccls::JsonReader::getPath
functions.description: Return a human-readable path into the JSON document representing the current location (built from path_). Useful for diagnostics.
requirements: this->path_ must contain valid C strings composing the path elements
Callable on a const JsonReader

functions.name: ccls::JsonWriter::startArray
functions.description: Begin a JSON array on the underlying RapidJSON writer.
requirements: m must be non-null and point to a valid JsonWriter::W instance

functions.name: ccls::JsonWriter::endArray
functions.description: End the current JSON array on the underlying writer.
requirements: A matching startArray() must have been called and not yet closed
m must be a valid writer pointer

functions.name: ccls::JsonWriter::startObject
functions.description: Begin a JSON object on the underlying RapidJSON writer.
requirements: m must be non-null and valid
Must be balanced with a subsequent endObject()

functions.name: ccls::JsonWriter::endObject
functions.description: End the current JSON object on the underlying writer.
requirements: A matching startObject() must have been called and not yet closed
m must be valid

functions.name: ccls::JsonWriter::key
functions.description: Write a JSON object member key to the writer. Typically followed by a value emission.

name must be a null-terminated UTF-8 string; pointer must remain valid for the call duration
m must be valid

functions.name: ccls::JsonWriter::null_
functions.description: Write a JSON null value.
requirements: m must be valid

functions.name: ccls::JsonWriter::int64

Call in a syntactically correct position (array element or object value)

functions.name: ccls::JsonWriter::string

requirements: s must be a non-null pointer to a null-terminated UTF-8 string

functions.name: ccls::MultiQueueLock::MultiQueueLock
functions.description: Constructs a composite lock over multiple queues/lockables and immediately locks all of them using std::lock. Used to create a Lockable object compatible with std::condition_variable_any.
requirements: Each argument in lockable must be a pointer or object for which std::get<Is>(tuple_)->mutex_ is valid; practically, each must point to/contain a public std::mutex member named mutex_.
None of the pointers may be null.
The referenced mutex_ objects must remain alive for the lifetime of this MultiQueueLock and across lock/unlock operations.
Lock acquisition may deadlock if arguments alias the same mutex or violate locking expectations.

functions.name: ccls::MultiQueueLock::~MultiQueueLock
functions.description: Destructor that unlocks all held mutexes acquired by the composite lock.
requirements: The underlying mutex_ members must still be alive when the destructor runs.

functions.name: ccls::MultiQueueLock::lock
functions.description: Locks all underlying mutex_ members using std::lock over the parameter pack. Exposed to satisfy the Lockable concept for use with condition_variable_any.
requirements: All queued objects must expose a mutex_ compatible with std::lock (i.e., std::mutex).
Calling lock() when already locked leads to undefined behavior analogous to double-locking std::mutex.

functions.name: ccls::MultiQueueLock::unlock
functions.description: Unlocks all underlying mutex_ members in a fold expression. Exposed to satisfy the Lockable concept for use with condition_variable_any.
requirements: Must be called only when the corresponding locks are currently held by this MultiQueueLock instance.
Underlying mutex_ objects must still be valid.

bool ccls::MultiQueueWaiter::wait(std::atomic<bool>& quit, BaseThreadQueue... queues)

Each argument in queues must be a pointer to a queue type that (1) derives from ccls::BaseThreadQueue (for isEmpty()), and (2) exposes a public std::mutex member named mutex_ (for locking).
All queue pointers must be non-null and remain valid for the duration of the call.

functions.signature:
template <class T>
template <void (std::deque<T>::*Push)(T&&)>
void ccls::ThreadedQueue<T>::push(T&& t, bool priority)
functions.description: Pushes an element to either the priority or normal queue using the provided std::deque member function pointer (e.g., push_back). Notifies one waiter after enqueuing.
requirements: Template argument Push must be a valid member function pointer of std::deque<T> with signature void (std::deque<T>::*)(T&&), such as &std::deque<T>::push_back or &std::deque<T>::push_front.

functions.description: Atomically removes and returns all elements from both the priority and normal queues, preserving the order within each (priority elements first, then normal). Resets the internal count to zero.
requirements: Caller receives ownership of returned elements by move; T must be movable.

functions.name: ccls::ThreadedQueue::isEmpty

functions.name: ccls::ThreadedQueue::dequeue
functions.description: Blocks until an element is available, then removes and returns the front element (preferring the priority queue). If keep_only_latest > 0, trims the selected queue to keep only the most recent keep_only_latest items before popping.
requirements: May block indefinitely until an element is available; should be called from a thread that can wait.
keep_only_latest must be >= 0; if > 0 and the selected queue has more than keep_only_latest elements, it erases older elements from the front.
T must be movable (element is returned by move).

functions.name: ccls::ThreadedQueue::tryPopFront
functions.description: Non-blocking pop of the front element, preferring the priority queue if non-empty. Returns std::nullopt if both queues are empty.
requirements: T must be movable (element is returned by move).

functions.signature:
template <class T>
template <typename Fn>
void ccls::ThreadedQueue<T>::apply(Fn fn)
functions.description: Invokes the provided callable with a reference to the normal queue's underlying std::deque<T> while holding the internal mutex. Allows custom in-place operations on the normal queue.
requirements: Fn must be callable as fn(std::deque<T>&).
The callable should not attempt to acquire the queue's mutex_ again or perform operations that would deadlock.
The callable should be fast to avoid blocking other operations.

functions.name: ccls::flattenHierarchy
functions.signature:
template <typename Node>
std::vector<Location> ccls::flattenHierarchy(const std::optional<Node>& root)
functions.description: Flattens a node hierarchy into a sorted, de-duplicated list of Location entries. If root is disengaged (std::nullopt), returns an empty vector. Otherwise, performs a breadth-first traversal starting from root->children (the root node itself is not included), collects each child’s location if it has a non-empty URI (location.uri.raw_uri.size() > 0), sorts the resulting Locations, and removes duplicates. Typical usage is to extract all unique source locations from a hierarchical structure (e.g., call/type hierarchy results) represented by Node objects compatible with this template.
requirements: Template type Node must provide: a member "children" that is an iterable container of Node elements and a member "location" whose type is convertible to ccls::Location.
Each child Node must itself have a "children" member (recursive structure) and a "location" member.
Node::location must have a nested structure with fields accessible as location.uri.raw_uri providing a size() method, used to test for a non-empty URI; only nodes with a non-empty URI are included.
The hierarchy referenced by root (and all nested children) must remain valid and not be modified concurrently during traversal (addresses of elements are taken and queued).
Location must be comparable (operator<) and equality comparable, as the function sorts and de-duplicates the result.
Passing std::nullopt for root is allowed and results in an empty vector.

functions.name: ccls::doPathMapping
functions.description: Applies the configured path mappings to the provided string in place. Intended to translate absolute paths embedded in arguments (e.g., compile_commands.json entries, .ccls options, or cache file paths) from one root to another using colon-separated mapping pairs (e.g., "/container:/host"). The function performs simple string replacement according to the configured mappings and does not return a value; the input string is modified directly. Exact replacement order and overlap behavior are not documented; details are inferred from the surrounding Config::Clang::pathMappings comments.
requirements: arg must be a valid, modifiable std::string; its contents may be changed in place.
Global configuration g_config must be initialized and accessible; if g_config->clang.pathMappings is empty, the call is effectively a no-op. (Inferred from usage pattern and surrounding comments.)

Mapping entries are colon-separated "from:to" pairs; replacement is simple string substitution as described in the comments for Config::Clang::pathMappings. (Exact matching rules beyond simple substitution are not specified.)
No return value; callers should inspect arg after the call to observe changes.
Thread-safety and concurrency guarantees are unknown; avoid concurrent calls that mutate shared state or the same string without external synchronization.

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Target format: NUL-terminated string located at the beginning of the buffer.
# The fuzzer stub ensures it copies bytes up to the first NUL and appends a NUL,
# then extra bytes. Our generator should produce an initial bytes buffer that is
# interesting yet valid as an input to FUZZ_PARAM_STR/FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME that
# ultimately becomes the start of a NUL-terminated C-string for BinaryReader::getString.
#
# Strategy:
# - Produce a variety of strings covering edge cases and common patterns.
# - Ensure they are valid to embed: bytes up to first NUL; include cases with
#   internal NUL early/late to exercise early termination behavior.
# - Include ASCII, extended bytes, path-like strings (for filename cases),
#   very short/empty, and near-boundary lengths.
# - Keep total size <= 4096 bytes.
#
# Note: The stub will append an explicit NUL and extra bytes, so our output does
# not need to include the terminator, but we may include internal NUL to test
# first-NUL termination logic.

def _rand_ascii(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    # Visible ASCII excluding NUL
    letters = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + string.punctuation + ' '
    return ''.join(rng.choice(letters) for _ in range(n)).encode('utf-8')

def _rand_bytes(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    # Any byte except we can include NUL intentionally sometimes
    return bytes(rng.randrange(0, 256) for _ in range(n))

def _make_path(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Generate POSIX/Windows-like path segments to exercise filename paths
    segments = []
    k = rng.randint(1, 5)
    for _ in range(k):
        seg_len = rng.randint(1, 10)
        seg = ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + '._-') for _ in range(seg_len))
        segments.append(seg)
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        # POSIX style
        s = '/' + '/'.join(segments)
    else:
        # Windows style
        drive = rng.choice('CDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ') + ':\\'
        s = drive + '\\'.join(segments)
    return s.encode('utf-8')

def _inject_internal_nul(rng: random.Random, data: bytes) -> bytes:
    if not data:
        return b"\x00"
    pos = rng.randint(0, len(data))  # allow at end -> acts like no early NUL effect in buf before explicit terminator
    return data[:pos] + b"\x00" + data[pos:]

def _build_candidates(rng: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    fixed_cases = [
        b"",  # empty string
        b"a",  # single char
        b"\x00",  # immediate terminator at first byte
        b"A" * 1,
        b"hello",
        b"foo/bar/baz",
        b"path\x00withrest",  # internal NUL early
        b"\xf0\x9f\x92\xa9",  # UTF-8 emoji pile of poo
    ]
    # Path-like
    cases = fixed_cases + [
        _make_path(rng),
        _make_path(rng) + (b"/" if rng.random() < 0.5 else b""),
    ]
    # Variable sizes including near 0, small, medium, and up to ~1024
    for length in [2, 3, 7, 15, 31, 63, 127, 255, 512, 1024]:
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            cases.append(_rand_ascii(rng, min(length, 1024)))
        else:
            # Mostly ASCII with some extended bytes
            base = _rand_ascii(rng, max(0, min(length - 4, 1024)))
            ext = _rand_bytes(rng, rng.randint(0, 4))
            mixed = bytearray(base)
            insert_pos = rng.randint(0, len(mixed)) if mixed else 0
            cases.append(bytes(mixed[:insert_pos] + ext + mixed[insert_pos:]))
    # Add some with internal NUL inserted at random positions
    augmented = []
    for c in cases:
        if rng.random() < 0.35:
            augmented.append(_inject_internal_nul(rng, c))
    cases.extend(augmented)
    # Deduplicate while preserving order
    seen = set()
    uniq = []
    for c in cases:
        if c not in seen:
            seen.add(c)
            uniq.append(c)
    return uniq

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    candidates = _build_candidates(rng)
    # Choose a candidate with a bias: occasionally pick extremes
    choice_pool = []
    if candidates:
        choice_pool.append(candidates[0])              # empty or first
        choice_pool.append(candidates[min(2, len(candidates)-1)])
        choice_pool.append(candidates[-1])             # last
    choice_pool.extend(rng.sample(candidates, k=min(5, len(candidates))))
    data = rng.choice(choice_pool) if choice_pool else b""

    # Ensure final size cap. The stub will append a NUL and extra 3 bytes, but our buffer
    # is fed to FUZZ_PARAM_STR, so it is unconstrained; still limit generously.
    if len(data) > 4000:
        data = data[:4000]

    # Return as bytes; FUZZ_PARAM_STR consumes std::string with arbitrary bytes.
    return data

import random
import struct
from typing import List

# This generator produces an interesting binary blob resembling what ccls::BinaryWriter
# might create: a sequence of varUInt, varInt encodings followed by a C-string payload.
# The fuzzer stub first emits a varUInt, then a varInt, then writes a C-string (bytes
# up to a NUL terminator). We will build buffers that:
# - Exercise all varUInt marker branches (<253, 16-bit, 32-bit, 64-bit)
# - Exercise varInt via zigzag for negative, zero, and positive values of varying magnitudes
# - Append a textual segment that is valid as a C-string (no embedded NUL) and NUL-terminated
# - Keep total size <= 4096 bytes

# Helper: encode varUInt with ccls::BinaryWriter scheme
# If n < 253: one byte n
# else if n < 65536: 253 then uint16
# else if n < 4294967296: 254 then uint32
# else: 255 then uint64

def _varuint(n: int) -> bytes:
    if n < 0:
        n &= (1 << 64) - 1  # treat as unsigned
    if n < 253:
        return bytes([n])
    elif n < 65536:
        return bytes([253]) + struct.pack('<H', n)
    elif n < 4294967296:
        return bytes([254]) + struct.pack('<I', n)
    else:
        return bytes([255]) + struct.pack('<Q', n & 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF)

# Helper: zigzag encode signed to unsigned, then varUInt
# zigzag: (n << 1) ^ (n >> 63) for 64-bit signed

def _varint(n: int) -> bytes:
    n &= 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF  # limit to 64-bit signed domain representation
    # interpret as signed 64 then zigzag
    if n & (1 << 63):
        signed = n - (1 << 64)
    else:
        signed = n
    zz = (signed << 1) ^ (signed >> 63)
    zz &= 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF
    return _varuint(zz)

# Build a C-string segment (bytes without NUL) plus a single NUL terminator at end.
# The ccls::BinaryWriter::string reserves len+1 and copies len bytes, so readers
# often expect a trailing NUL sitting in the buffer contents following the copied bytes.

def _c_string_payload(rng: random.Random, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    # Use a mix of ASCII, path-like, JSON-like and code-like tokens; avoid NUL inside.
    token_pool = [
        "include <vector>",
        "int main() { return 0; }",
        "C:/Proj/Path/File.hpp",
        "/usr/local/include/ccls/config.json",
        "namespace::Class::method",
        "UTF8-✓-测试-данные",
        "foo/bar/baz_qux-123",
        "--flag -DNAME=VALUE -Iinclude",
        "{\"key\":\"value\"}",
        "hello_world.cpp",
    ]
    # Assemble 1..k tokens joined by separators
    parts: List[str] = []
    total_target = rng.randint(8, max(8, max_len))
    while parts and sum(len(p) for p in parts) < total_target and len(parts) < 8:
        parts.append(rng.choice(token_pool))
        parts.append(rng.choice([" ", ",", ";", "|", ":", " "]))
    if not parts:
        parts.append(rng.choice(token_pool))
    s = ''.join(parts)
    s = s[:max_len]
    # Ensure no embedded NULs
    b = s.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore').replace(b"\x00", b"?")
    return b + b"\x00"

# Compose a buffer covering diverse varUInt/varInt cases in one blob.

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    out = bytearray()

    # Plan a sequence similar to stub: at least one varUInt, one varInt, and a C-string.
    # We will prepend multiple pairs to exercise different branches.
    def add_varuint_cases():
        # Values to hit thresholds: <253, 16-bit, 32-bit, 64-bit
        cases = [
            rng.randrange(0, 253),            # single byte
            rng.randrange(253, 65536),        # 16-bit path
            rng.randrange(65536, 0x100000000),# 32-bit path
            rng.getrandbits(64),              # 64-bit path
        ]
        rng.shuffle(cases)
        for v in cases:
            out.extend(_varuint(v))

    def add_varint_cases():
        # Craft signed values: negative small, zero, positive small, large negative, large positive
        signed_cases = [
            -rng.randint(1, 200),
            0,
            rng.randint(1, 200),
            -(1 << rng.randint(20, 40)),
            (1 << rng.randint(20, 40)),
        ]
        rng.shuffle(signed_cases)
        for v in signed_cases:
            out.extend(_varint(v & 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF))

    add_varuint_cases()
    add_varint_cases()

    # Append several C-string segments; the stub writes once, but extra strings are valid blob data
    # and help downstream consumers that may read multiple strings.
    remaining = 4096 - len(out)
    str_count = rng.randint(1, 4)
    for _ in range(str_count):
        max_len = max(4, min(128, remaining - 2))
        if max_len <= 4:
            break
        cstr = _c_string_payload(rng, max_len)
        # Ensure not to exceed size bound
        if len(out) + len(cstr) > 4096:
            break
        out.extend(cstr)
        remaining = 4096 - len(out)

    return bytes(out)

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Data type: arbitrary text (UTF-8/byte string) used for logging/display.
# Fuzzer stub uses FUZZ_PARAM_STR to feed a std::string into an ostringstream.
# Provide varied but valid UTF-8-ish content, including different lengths,
# whitespace, punctuation, Unicode, and typical log-like patterns. Avoid
# exceeding 4096 bytes.

UNICODE_BLOCKS = [
    # Common ASCII printable set
    ''.join(chr(i) for i in range(0x20, 0x7f)),
    # Whitespace and control that are typically safe in text logs
    "\t\n\r \x0b\x0c",
    # Latin-1 supplement selection
    "àáâãäåæçèéêëìíîïðñòóôõö÷øùúûüýþÿ",
    # Cyrillic sample
    "Приветмир",
    # Greek sample
    "ΑλφαΒηταΓαμμαΔελτα",
    # Emojis
    "🙂🙃😉🔥💡🐍✈️🚀📦🧪",
    # CJK sample
    "测试中文漢字かなカナ日本語",
]

LOG_PREFIXES = [
    "INFO:", "WARN:", "ERROR:", "DEBUG:", "TRACE:", "NOTICE:", "FATAL:",
]

SUFFIXES = [
    " end", "", " [ok]", " [fail]", " (#1)", " ::done", " ::pending",
]

SPECIAL_LINES = [
    "key=value", "path:/usr/local/bin", "user:alice id=42", "token:abcdef123456",
    "{" + "msg: test" + "}", "[section] name=example", ""  # empty string option
]

def _rand_ascii(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> str:
    alphabet = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + string.punctuation + ' '
    return ''.join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))

def _weighted_choice(rng: random.Random, items: List[str]) -> str:
    return rng.choice(items)

def _make_log_like(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    prefix = _weighted_choice(rng, LOG_PREFIXES)
    block = rng.choice(UNICODE_BLOCKS)
    # Random middle part composed from several chunks
    chunks = []
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 4)):
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            # slice of a unicode block
            start = rng.randrange(0, max(1, len(block)))
            end = min(len(block), start + rng.randint(1, 8))
            chunks.append(block[start:end])
        else:
            chunks.append(_rand_ascii(rng, rng.randint(3, 12)))
    mid = ' '.join(chunks)
    suf = _weighted_choice(rng, SUFFIXES)
    # Optionally include newlines or tabs
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        mid += "\n" + _rand_ascii(rng, rng.randint(5, 20))
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        mid = mid.replace(' ', "\t", 1)
    return f"{prefix} {mid}{suf}"

def _make_multiline(rng: random.Random, max_bytes: int) -> str:
    lines = []
    for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 6)):
        pick = rng.random()
        if pick < 0.4:
            lines.append(_make_log_like(rng))
        elif pick < 0.7:
            lines.append(_weighted_choice(rng, SPECIAL_LINES))
        else:
            lines.append(_rand_ascii(rng, rng.randint(5, 40)))
    s = "\n".join(lines)
    # Truncate to max_bytes safely (UTF-8 slicing; since we build from str, slicing is code point safe)
    if len(s.encode('utf-8')) > max_bytes:
        # truncate by characters until byte size fits
        enc = s.encode('utf-8')[:max_bytes]
        # ensure valid utf-8 by decoding with ignore (fuzzer accepts arbitrary text; valid std::string is fine)
        s = enc.decode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
    return s

def _make_payload(rng: random.Random, max_bytes: int) -> str:
    mode = rng.random()
    if mode < 0.25:
        # Simple short token
        return _rand_ascii(rng, rng.randint(0, 32))
    elif mode < 0.55:
        # Log-like single line
        s = _make_log_like(rng)
        if len(s.encode('utf-8')) > max_bytes:
            s = s[:max_bytes]
        return s
    else:
        # Multiline mixture
        return _make_multiline(rng, max_bytes)

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Choose target size up to 1024 bytes to stay well under 4096, but vary distribution
    target = rng.choice([64, 128, 256, 512, 1024, rng.randint(5, 4000)])
    s = _make_payload(rng, target)
    # Occasionally pad or prepend with unicode/control to vary formatting
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        pad = rng.choice(["\n", "\t", " ", "\r\n"])
        s = pad + s
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        endpad = rng.choice(["\n", "", "\n\n", " "])
        s = s + endpad
    b = s.encode('utf-8', errors='strict')
    if len(b) > 4096:
        b = b[:4096]
    return b
